title: operatorized-evacuation-and-rollback-sequences: add evacuation-operator, terraform module, helm hooks
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ and air-gapped datacenters asked for a repeatable, auditable operator-driven evacuation and rollback flow that can be executed as code and integrated into DR rehearsals. This PR introduces an "evacuation-operator" CRD + controller that codifies multi-stage evacuations (drain, KV snapshot, traffic cutover, rehydrate) with a dry-run/simulate mode, and ties it to terraform modules and Helm chart hooks so on-prem and VPC installs can opt-in with minimal manual steps.

What this changes: adds a new Kubernetes operator and CRD (evac.redwood.ai/v1alpha1 EvacuationPlan), a terraform module redwood_private_failover that generates pre-signed job manifests and control-plane ACLs, and Helm chart lifecycle hooks (preStop/preStart) to coordinate safe draining and consistency checks. Includes a runbook-as-code manifest library (yaml + templated runbooks) used by the operator to emit staged notifications and to produce an execution audit trail.

Design notes: the operator implements idempotent stages and uses leader election so only one controller runs per cluster. There is an optional "simulate_traffic_replay" flag which replays recorded request traces (redwood/drill-traces) against a local canary to verify behavior before committing cutover. For stateful components we added snapshot+transfer steps for ETCD and Postgres logical replication slots. Rollback sequences are modeled as the inverse of the evacuation plan with explicit validation gates.

Checklist: [x] CRD + controller code; [x] helm chart patches + lifecycle hooks; [x] terraform module scaffold + examples; [x] runbook-as-code templates; [x] CI e2e canary; [x] docs draft (internal runbook).

Compatibility: default behavior is opt-in; no changes to existing installs unless users enable the evacuation operator or use the terraform module. Migration steps included for clusters that want to adopt the operator over manual scripts.

Notes on tests and rollout: e2e uses a small metal3 cluster in CI that runs the dry-run mode; we have a separate integration test that runs the full sequence in a sandboxed ON-PREM lab. We observed one flaky 'helm-posthooks' test in CI caused by timing of preStop hooks; CI retry is wired in the pipeline.

Related work: touches private installer, helm charts, and terraform modules; followups planned to add RBAC policy bundling for remote operators and to integrate with the console's DR dashboard (ENG-4821).

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Can the operator run in read-only dry-run mode without cluster-admin? We should document required RBAC for each feature.
Asha Patel (author): Dry-run only requires limited discover/list/watch permissions; full execution needs elevated perms. Added RBAC doc and least-privilege matrix in README.
Evelyn Zhang: Postgres logical replication step looks asynchronous; add status conditions and timeouts so rollbacks won't block indefinitely.
Asha Patel (author): Added status conditions and configurable timeouts; default 30m for snapshot transfer and a 'force-fail' gate for emergency aborts.
Ravi Kumar: Terraform examples should include a minimal VPC example to make adoption easier for on-prem mirror setups.
Asha Patel (author): Added simple VPC example workspace and an ops note on network ACL expectations.
requested_changes: Ravi Kumar requested minimal terraform example (addressed)
Security review pending re: operator exec permissions (accepted risk; mitigations added)
release_notes: Added an opt-in evacuation operator and runbook-as-code templates to automate multi-AZ evacuation, snapshot, and rollback sequences for Private deployments. Includes a terraform module to bootstrap failover artifacts and Helm lifecycle hooks for safe drains. Opt-in only; no behavioral change until enabled.
notes: This PR is intended to be reviewed with the runbook YAMLs and terraform example workspace. We plan a staged rollout in partner labs during Q1 2026. Follow-up PR will add Console integration for plan visualization and an RBAC policy bundle for operator-only service accounts.
